tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.lv_dis: A 10-block treated wood pole for LV lines: three pin insulators on its crossarm (A, B, C) and the neutral (N) on a bracket below it. Hang a Pole-Mount Transformer on it for split phase.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.mv_sub: A 15-block treated wood pole for MV lines: three porcelain post insulators (A, B, C) on two crossarms, and a shield wire peak on top.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.hv_h_f: A 21-block H-frame of two treated wood poles for HV lines: three glass suspension strings (A, B, C) hung from its crossbeam.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.ehv_la: A 32-block galvanized steel lattice tower for EHV lines: two circuits, each three glass suspension strings (A, B, C) hung from its crossarms.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.pin_in: One insulator, one conductor's end. Mount it on any face of a block to move FE between the block and the grid. All the pin insulators on one block make one port, which needs a whole circuit: A, B and C, or a line and N. Wrench: Configure steps the mode (input, output, storage: a grid-tied battery), Sneak + Configure the current limit, Rotate the phase, Port the circuit type.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.wire_c: One bare conductor. Use it on an insulator, then on another of the same tier, to string a wire between them. Sneak-use in the air lets go of the loose end. Keep a wire under its rated current, or it burns out. Live bare wire shocks whatever touches it: LV stings, MV takes a quarter of your health, HV half, EHV kills.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.pole_t: Hang it on the side of a pole. Links three-phase LV on its lid (A, B, C) to split phase on its front (L1, N, L2), either way, holding none.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.burnt_: What's left of a wire that carried more than its rating for too long. Smelts down to a copper nugget.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.wire_c: Use them on a wire to cut it, or on an insulator to cut every wire on it. The wire's coil drops where it was cut.
death.attack.arcforgetransmission.electr: %1$s touched a live wire while fighting %2$s
death.attack.arcforgetransmission.barbed: %1$s was caught on barbed wire escaping %2$s
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.mv_sub: Links an MV line (its north bushings) to an LV line (its south bushings), three-phase both sides: power passes whichever way the grid needs, and it holds none. Its load tap changer holds the low side's voltage; Wrench on Configure holds it or lets it run.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.hv_sub: Links an HV line (its north bushings) to an MV line (its south bushings), three-phase both sides: power passes whichever way the grid needs, and it holds none. Its load tap changer holds the low side's voltage; Wrench on Configure holds it or lets it run.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.ehv_su: Links an EHV line (its north bushings) to an HV line (its south bushings), three-phase both sides: power passes whichever way the grid needs, and it holds none. Its load tap changer holds the low side's voltage; Wrench on Configure holds it or lets it run.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.unit_t: Links a three-phase line (A, B, C on its lid) to the FE blocks touching its front, the side its cable box faces. Wrench on Configure: Input (generators onto the line; one that pushes FE can push into any of its blocks), Output (feeds machines, at any voltage) or Storage (a battery in front: it covers what the grid's sources can't, and charges from what they have spare).
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.wall_b: Passes wires through a wall. Mount Pin Insulators on its faces: those of one tier and phase are joined through it, so a run comes in one side and leaves the other. Takes an Arcforge Conduit Facade: use a block on the facade to dress it in that block's look.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.insula: Rubber-insulated wire: safe to touch, unlike bare wire, which shocks anything touching it while live. Use it on an insulator, then on another of the same tier, to string a wire.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.bauxit: Aluminium ore. Mine it for Raw Bauxite; smelt that into Aluminium Ingots, or crush it in an Arc Crusher for more dust.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.deepsl: Aluminium ore. Mine it for Raw Bauxite; smelt that into Aluminium Ingots, or crush it in an Arc Crusher for more dust.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.raw_ba: Smelt it into an Aluminium Ingot, or crush it in an Arc Crusher for Aluminium Dust.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.alumin: Light and conductive: MV wire is drawn from it.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.raw_ba: Nine Raw Bauxite, packed. Crush it in an Arc Crusher for Aluminium Dust.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.wire.shield: Grounded steel for the tower peaks (G): catches lightning
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.wire.buried: Underground: insulated, never drawn, out of lightning's reach
message.arcforgetransmission.wire.shield: Shield wire goes on a tower's peak (G) only
That's a shield point (G): use Shield Wire
message.arcforgetransmission.meter.wire: %s %s: %s A of %s A (%s%%) · loss %s FE/t · %s blocks · %s–%s
message.arcforgetransmission.guy.tied: Guy tied to the pole: now use it on the ground
message.arcforgetransmission.guy.too_far: Too far, too high or too many: a guy runs down to the ground within reach
hud.arcforgetransmission.fuse.blown: Fuse blown: use a Fuse Link
hud.arcforgetransmission.breaker.lockout: Locked out: close it by hand
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.fuse_c: One conductor's fuse, hung beside a pole: wire its top (line) and bottom (load). Over its rating its element heats, melting fast at fault current and slowly just over, opening the line; put it back with a Fuse Link. Wrench on Rotate changes its phase.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.reclos: Three-phase protection: its north bushings (line) joined to its south ones (load) while closed. Over its trip setting it trips (graded: the device nearest the trouble goes first), recloses, and after its last try locks out. Empty hand opens or closes it; Wrench on Configure sets its trip current. Fit a CT and link a Relay Panel for an inverse curve.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.circui: Three-phase protection: its north bushings (line) joined to its south ones (load) while closed. Over its trip setting it trips (graded: the device nearest the trouble goes first), recloses, and after its last try locks out. Empty hand opens or closes it; Wrench on Configure sets its trip current. Fit a CT and link a Relay Panel for an inverse curve.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.discon: Opens a three-phase line by hand (empty hand): a visible break. Everything past an open switch is dead, so its bare wire is safe to touch.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.dead_e: Ends a line both ways, or turns it a corner: strain insulators on each side, each conductor jumpered through. Place it at 45 degrees for a corner, and guy it.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.servic: A building's service: tie L1, N and L2 from a Pole-Mount Transformer's secondary to its spools, and it feeds the FE block it faces, counting what it delivers.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.surge_: Place it within a few blocks of a transformer: a lightning surge on its line won't destroy it.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.fuse_l: Use it on a blown Fuse Cutout to put it back.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.clamp_: Use it at a wire (or on an insulator) to read its current, rating, loss and length.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.guy_wi: Use it on a pole, then on the ground, to guy it. Sneak-use on the pole to take the last guy off.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.shield: Steel strung between the towers' peaks (their G points) over a line: lightning strikes it, not the conductors.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.underg: Insulated cable run underground: never drawn, safe to touch, and out of lightning's reach.
Storage (a battery: covers the shortfall, takes the surplus)
message.arcforgetransmission.interlock.l: Interlocked: a ground switch is closed on this line
message.arcforgetransmission.fitting.can: Nothing here for that to measure
message.arcforgetransmission.control.tie: Control Cable tied: now use it on what to link
message.arcforgetransmission.control.can: Those don't link: a Relay Panel to a breaker, bank, reactor or substation transformer; a Disconnect Switch to its breaker
message.arcforgetransmission.control.too: Too far apart (%s blocks at most)
hud.arcforgetransmission.bus: Bus: joined to the sections in line with it
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.mv_dis: Hang it on the side of a pole. Links an MV feeder (A, B, C on its lid) to split phase LV on its front (L1, N, L2): houses straight off an MV line.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.bus: Rigid pipe bus on glass station posts: one node a phase that every wire on it shares. Sections placed in a row, two blocks apart along the line, join up.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.dead_e: Brings lines into a yard: each phase dead-ends on the girder's north face and drops, jumpered, to a string on its south side for the yard's wiring. Shield peaks on its legs.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.voltag: Joins its north bushings (source) to its south ones (load) through its boost, stepping its tap (up to 10% either way) to hold the load side's voltage. Wrench on Configure holds its tap or lets it run.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.relay_: Link it with Control Cable to the breakers it protects (each with a CT fitted): an inverse-time curve, an instantaneous element and lost-phase and unbalance tripping; to capacitor banks and reactors (a PT fitted) to switch them on the voltage; and to a substation transformer (a CT fitted) for differential protection against lightning. Wrench on Configure: its time dial; sneaking, fuse-saving or fuse-blowing.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.ground: Grounds its line while closed (empty hand), so a dead line stays dead: no shock, no back-feed. It only closes on a dead line, and a breaker won't close onto it.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.capaci: A shunt capacitor bank on its three bushings: switched in, it raises the voltage near it. Empty hand or redstone switches it; a Relay Panel (a PT fitted) switches it on the voltage.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.shunt_: A shunt reactor on its three bushings: switched in, it lowers the voltage near it. Empty hand or redstone switches it; a Relay Panel (a PT fitted) switches it on the voltage.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.dead_e: Ends a line both ways or turns it a corner under tension: glass strain strings off both faces, each conductor jumpered through. Place it at 45 degrees for a corner.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.transp: A dead-end tower whose jumpers cross: each conductor comes in at one place and leaves a place over, so the phases rotate along the line.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.cable_: Where an overhead line goes underground: wire its terminations (top) to the line and Underground Cable from its cable box (at its foot), each conductor joined through.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.sectio: Counts the recloser's operations behind it (fault current, then the line going dead) and opens in the dead time after its count, isolating a lasting fault beyond it. It can't break current itself. Close it by hand.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.transf: Its load (south row) on its preferred feeder (north row), changed over to its alternate (middle row) once the preferred has been dead a moment, and back once it's been live a while. Empty hand changes it over.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.statio: Fence a substation yard with it: a fault inside gives step-potential shocks to anything standing near, unless Ground Grid lies under it.

Goes on top of a Station Fence (only there), leaning outward the way you look as you place it (Wrench on Rotate turns it). Its strands join along the fence and round its corners; nothing jumps it, and touching it pricks.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.ground: Lay it under a yard: within its reach of a fault the ground stays even, so no one standing there is shocked.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.curren: Fit it to a breaker or substation transformer (use it on one) for a Relay Panel to read its current.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.potent: Fit it to a breaker, transformer or capacitor bank (use it on one) for a Relay Panel to read its voltage.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.contro: Use it on a Relay Panel, then on what it protects or switches; or on a Disconnect Switch, then its breaker (the interlock). Again to unlink. Not used up.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.cable_: Where a tray cable ends: a whole circuit (A, B and C) in one block. Mount it on any face of a block: on a machine it's that block's port, set like a Pin Insulator (Wrench: Configure the mode, Sneak + Configure the current limit); on a lineup section or busway tap-off it joins the cable through. Rotate swaps B and C; Port switches an LV one to L1, N and L2. HV stands 2 blocks tall, EHV 3.
hud.arcforgetransmission.cable_terminati: Joined through what it's mounted on
message.arcforgetransmission.cable_termi: Only an LV termination can be split-phase
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.incomi: Where a lineup's circuit comes in: overhead wires on its bushings, or a tray cable on a Cable Termination mounted on it. LV and MV: a load-break switch with current-limiting fuses; HV and EHV: a breaker with its disconnector and earthing switch (interlocked). Place a lineup's sections side by side, facing the same way: Incoming, (Transformer), Main Breaker, Feeders (a Bus Tie between two halves).
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.transf: Steps a lineup's bus one tier down, rated one full circuit of its tier. Fans come on over 100% and let it carry up to 133%; past that it heats, and trips its incomer on over-temperature (its HUD shows its temperature). Wrench on Configure: its off-load tap, only with its incomer open.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.main_s: One breaker between the incomer (or transformer) and the lineup's bus, its frame sized to what feeds it. Wrench on Configure steps its trip unit's setting, Sneak + Configure picks long-time, short-time or instantaneous. It won't close onto a faulted bus.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.feeder: Feeder breakers off the lineup's bus (two a section at LV and MV, one a bay at HV and EHV). Each leaves by a Cable Termination on its block, or (the upper) a busway feed-in on the roof. Wrench on Configure steps the nearest breaker's frame. Graded with the main: the feeder nearest a fault trips, the main holds.
tooltip.arcforgetransmission.info.tie_se: Joins a double-ended lineup's two bus halves; normally open. Lose an incomer and close the tie (by hand or redstone) to carry both halves from the other. The two mains and the tie can't all be closed at once.
message.arcforgetransmission.lineup.eart: Earthing switch closed: the line is earthed
message.arcforgetransmission.lineup.bus_: The bus is faulted or earthed: clear it first
message.arcforgetransmission.lineup.para: Both mains and the tie can't all be closed: open one first
message.arcforgetransmission.lineup.open: Open the incomer first: the taps change only off-load
hud.arcforgetransmission.lineup.too_many: too many Feeder Sections on a bus half
hud.arcforgetransmission.lineup.tie_tier: its halves' buses are at different tiers
